additionalCoursework:
Completion of humanities coursework is recommended in order to prepare students to meet the needs of underserved communities.

Recommended coursework includes the following:
English, writing, composition, logic, or critical thinking — Eight (8) semester hours in any English, writing, composition, logic, or critical thinking courses.
Humanities/social sciences — Eight (8) semester hours.
Spanish — Three (3) semester hours.

Applicants are encouraged to review the recommended program prerequisites category for more information about recommended coursework.

medSchoolStudLife.diversity: The UC Riverside School of Medicine is committed to recognizing and nurturing merit, talent and achievement by supporting diversity and equal opportunity within every aspect of the School.  Several pathway programs exist that provide support, guidance and resources to prospective students from groups traditionally underrepresented in medicine. Recruitment efforts and resources will be aligned with the goal to recruit qualified individuals from groups underrepresented in medicine into faculty positions, recognizing that faculty, in particular, serve as role models to attract a diverse student body. For additional information on student pathway programs, please see: https://pathwayprograms.ucr.edu/
medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence: On a case-by-case basis, the Senior Associate Dean of Student Affairs will make the decision to approve or disapprove requests for a leave of absence.
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities:
Medical students have the opportunity to participate in a variety of programs which include the Inland Empire Street Medicine, and Coachella Valley Free Clinics, the Wellness Program, Careers in Medicine, One-to-One Faculty Mentoring Program, Medical Student Special Lecture Series, Student Interest groups and the Big Brother/Big Sister Program.  Students are also invited to participate in the SOM formal outreach efforts to mentor K-12, undergraduate or post-baccalaureate students, or work on community projects with the Mini-Medical School health education program.

For additional information on student interest groups and activities, please see: https://somsa.ucr.edu/student-interest-groups
medSchoolStudLife.setting: The UCR School of Medicine is located on the University of California, Riverside main campus in Inland Southern California, approximately 60 miles east of downtown Los Angeles.  Located on nearly 1,200 acres near Box Springs Mountain, the park-like campus provides convenient access to the vibrant and growing Inland Southern California region, a metropolitan area with a population of approximately 4 million people.
medSchoolStudLife.housing: UCR offers a diverse selection of housing opportunities, including family student housing, campus apartments and residence halls. Ample off campus accommodations are also available within walking distance, and public transportation is available to nearby students as well.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystems: Established in 1993, the LGBT Resource Center provides support, education, and advocacy regarding sexual orientation and gender identity/expression for the UC Riverside community and beyond. For additional information on campus support systems for gender and sexual minority students, please see: https://out.ucr.edu/
medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms:
The SOM Office of Student Support and Wellness at the UCR School of Medicine works to improve and nurture the overall mental health and wellbeing of our students by offering a variety of training and resources. These tools allow students to approach their wellbeing from a whole health perspective and will help them develop balanced habits that can be used throughout their lives.

The office provides a safe space for students to talk about their mental health and wellness concerns, provide personal wellness planning, adjust to clerkship experiences, and help students prepare for exams. For additional information on wellness programs, please see: https://somsa.ucr.edu/office-student-support-wellness
medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture: At UC Riverside, belonging, community, connection, and a vibrant campus life are central to the campus experience. Once a Highlander you are always a member of our community.
medSchoolStudLife.transportationAdditionalInfo: Students are recommended to have reliable transportation.

medSchoolCurriculum.dressCode: Dress code is casual for lectures and business casual for the skills based courses and clinically based activities.
medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms: Tutoring is available for all medical students.  The staff and faculty within the Office of Student Affairs work proactively to assist students in identifying academic difficulty early on.
medSchoolCurriculum.patientInteraction: Students begin their patient interaction in the first month of Year 1.
medSchoolCurriculum.instructionStyle: The instruction style is primarily didactic and small group discussions.
medSchoolCurriculum.clinicalRotations: Clinical Rotations begin during the third year.
medSchoolCurriculum.lectureAttendance: Lectures are not mandatory; All active learning sessions require attendance.
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights:
Instruction in the first year uses an integrated approach to understanding human biological systems, and the second year places emphasis on disease processes. Starting in the first year, students will participate in a three-year Longitudinal Ambulatory Care Experience (LACE) where they will begin seeing a panel of patients under the supervision of a physician-mentor. LACE continues through the third year, providing sustained clinical exposure that emphasizes the application of core clinical competencies, continuity of care, and a seamless transition from pre-clerkship to clerkship training.

LACE also integrates the Clinical Reasoning Thread and the Health Systems Science Project (HSSP). Together, these components reinforce how foundational scientific knowledge informs diagnostic reasoning and patient care, while fostering scientific inquiry, innovation, and community-informed research inspired by students’ real-world clinical experiences.
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms: An emphasis on primary care is a fundamental component of the mission of the UCR School of Medicine.  As such, the focus of clinical training will be on ambulatory primary care to the fullest extent possible while ensuring that the educational curriculum prepares students to pursue further training in any discipline of medicine. Each clinical component of the curriculum has been designed to emphasize both the core content of that discipline as well as its relationship with primary care.  The UCR School of Medicine will emphasize the central role primary care plays in coordinating specialty care and in providing the continuity before and after episodes of specialty care.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms: Research opportunities for students are available in the laboratories of the full-time faculty in the School of Medicine and in many laboratories and centers across the main UC Riverside campus.  Additional research opportunities are available through clinical researchers and community-based participatory research projects in Inland Southern California. Students may work on any of these research projects during the summer break between the first and second year. In addition, some students may elect to take a leave from their SOM education to pursue longer research projects (on or off campus), including doctoral degree programs. All students will be strongly encouraged to participate in a scholarly project.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchThesisText: Each student is required to complete a health systems science project over 3 yrs as part of their LACE experience. Students are required to present the research at the Dean's MD Student Research Day.
medSchoolCurriculum.affiliatedHospitals: We have partnered with Riverside University Health System, Kaiser Permanente Medical Center-Riverside, Desert Regional Medical Center, Riverside Community Hospital in addition to others.
medSchoolCurriculum.gradingSystem:
Pass/Fail grading system in Pre-clinical years
Honors/High Pass/Pass/Fail in third year
Pass/Fail grading system in fourth year

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation:
UC Riverside has built its medical school from a long history of training physicians in partnership with UCLA's David Geffen School of Medicine. Now an independent four-year program, the UCR School of Medicine is poised to meet the region's physician workforce needs and improve the health of the population it serves. The medical school offers a program of ambulatory-based, patient-centered, medical home-oriented and culturally competent physician training focused on wellness and preventive care.

The school will also expand UCR's existing strength in basic biomedical and other health-related sciences research to include building research expertise in population health and health outcomes.  Through its research, the medical school will address specific health care challenges within Inland Southern California, serving as a catalyst for improving the health of people living in the region.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement: The mission of the UCR School of Medicine is to improve the health of the people of California and, especially, to serve Inland Southern California by training a diverse workforce of physicians and by developing innovative research and health care delivery programs that will improve the health of the medically underserved in the region and become models to be emulated throughout the state and nation.

medSchoolApplication.amcasLettersText: We require a minimum of 3 letters of recommendation.  The committee will accept no more than 5 letters total.  We ask that you abide by the 5 letter limit. Applicants submitting committee letters that include at least three original letters in their entirety will meet the minimum letter requirement.
medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance: Letters of recommendation may be written by a premedical advisor, undergraduate faculty, mentor or any individual of your choice. Letters must be original, signed documents on institutional letterhead and be submitted by Nov. 1st, 2026.
medSchoolApplication.typicalInterviewDay: Upon invitation, applicants will receive a school overview and the opportunity to interact virtually with the UCRSOM community, including faculty, staff, and students. To ensure a smooth experience, applicants will be provided with comprehensive manuals and dedicated staff support to assist with MMI experience.
medSchoolApplication.interviewFormat: Interviews will be scheduled on selected weekdays, weeknights, and weekends from September 2026 through March 2027. They will be conducted in the Multiple Mini-Interview (MMI) format.
medSchoolApplication.videoInterview: Interviews will be done virtually utilizing Zoom and KIRA.
medSchoolApplication.secApplSentTo: All verified applicants meeting eligibility will be notified by e-mail to complete a secondary application.
medSchoolApplication.ctsRequired: Out of state applicants will be considered on a case-by-case basis and only if they have demonstrated strong ties to inland southern California.
medSchoolApplication.acceptOutstateApplInformation: Out of state applicants will be considered on a case-by-case basis; Applicants will be considered only if they have demonstrated strong ties to inland southern California
medSchoolApplication.dacaDetail: The California Dream Act passed in 2011 gives undocumented DACA (AB540 eligibility students) access to state financial aid and institutional and privately-funded scholarships.
medSchoolApplication.additionalInfo:
Students are offered an interview based on their AMCAS application and their secondary application. Candidates selected for interviews will be notified by e-mail. At this stage, only those candidates who have been interviewed can be considered for admission.

Decisions for admissions are made on a rolling basis. Acceptances will continue until the class is full. Admission is provisional until candidates complete all required program requirements. Admission decisions are final and thus are not subject to appeal. A student not admitted as a result of the first application may file a second application the following year, however a third application cycle is strongly discouraged. An applicant may request a deferral for up to one year by writing to the Admissions Office. The decision to grant the deferral is made on an individual basis.

***Response to COVID-19 Information for 2026-2027 Admissions Cycle***

The purpose of this message is to address concerns from prospective applicants who are experiencing unprecedented educational upheaval during the COVID-19 pandemic.  Applicants for the upcoming application cycle can count on our commitment to the following principles:

Pass/Fail Grades – The UCR SOM will accept pass/fail grades, without prejudice, for courses taken during the COVID-19 pandemic.  It has always been our practice to consider grades in the context of numerous other aspects of the application, and an international crisis certainly provides a unique and compelling context.  In making this statement, we are cognizant of the fact that some undergraduate schools are providing an option for students to take courses either for grades or on a Pass/Fail basis. We therefore want to be explicit that applicants should not feel pressured by us to choose the graded option.  

Online Coursework– The faculty of the UCR SOM require that students demonstrate a strong foundation that indicates preparedness to engage the curriculum.  Our preparation areas are required, however we recognize that there is an increasing degree of variety in premedical course tracks and course offerings at colleges and universities.  We further recognize that students may meet these competencies through alternative means or courses, including online.  On our secondary application we invite applicants to explain and describe how they have met the requirements through course work and/or additional means.  The committee will NOT systematically disqualify candidates due to variation in course completion.  The committee will holistically evaluate the preparation of candidates for the school of medicine with a strong focus on science foundation and professional competencies.
medSchoolApplication.mcatScoresAdditionalInfo: The admissions committee considers the highest total MCAT score taken within the last 3 years. Applicants who plan to retake the MCAT exam should submit their new score by no later than November 1, 2026. Applicants who plan to take the MCAT exam for the first time should submit their new score by no later than November 1, 2026.
medSchoolApplication.minUndergradGpaInfo: We utilize holistic review and consider GPA's on a case-by-case basis.
medSchoolApplication.minCreditHourInfo: We utilize holistic review and we consider credit hours on a case-by-case basis.
medSchoolApplication.courseworkAcceptanceInfo:
We accept coursework completed at a community college to meet our required science core and recommended humanities core program pre-requisites. 

Detailed information about our minimum coursework requirements can be found here: https://somsa.ucr.edu/program-prerequisites
medSchoolApplication.letterOfIntentAdditionalInfo: Applicants are permitted to submit one (1) letter of intent, letter of interest, or notice of significant updates or achievements per admissions cycle. Applicants who complete an interview are permitted to submit one additional letter or notification.
medSchoolApplication.technicalStandardInfo: All interviewees must sign an acknowledgment of the UCR School of Medicine Technical Standards. This attestation is also a required step in the pre-matriculation process for all admitted students.

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid: The Financial Aid Counselor is available to assist students with financial planning for medical school. Scholarships and loans are available and are awarded on the basis of financial need and academic performance.

medSchoolPrograms.info:
Thomas Haider: The Thomas Haider Program at the UCR School of Medicine provides a unique pathway into medical school for at least 24 qualifying UC Riverside undergraduate students.

Thomas Haider Early Assurance Program (EAP): The Thomas Haider EAP program is a unique portal into the UCR School of Medicine 's Thomas Haider Program. It provides qualified, "mission-fit" UC Riverside undergraduate students or recent graduates with a guaranteed seat in a future UCR School of Medicine class one year after selection.

PRIME: The Program in Medical Education (PRIME) is designed to produce physicians who are specifically trained to address the healthcare needs of the African, Black, and Caribbean (ABC) communities of Inland Southern California. 

Conditional Admittance (CA) Program: The program is designed to recruit applicants who have demonstrated commitment to underserved communities in Inland Southern California but require additional preparation to be successful in medical school.

medSchoolSelection.premedReqRec:
All applicants must have a bachelor’s degree from a regionally-accredited US institution prior to matriculation. Students must complete all premedical requirements before beginning the first year of medical study, although these requirements need not be completed at the time application for admission is filed. Verification of completion of program pre-requisites will be done after you have been admitted.

Although students must complete the required pre-medical coursework, students are not required to be science majors to do so. The degree, to include required pre-requisite coursework, must have been completed at a regionally-accredited US institution. We value broad academic backgrounds that include humanities, foreign language, social sciences and the arts to help prepare future physicians for interacting with increasingly diverse patient populations, health care professionals and colleagues.
medSchoolSelection.oldestPrereqDate: The UCR SOM recommends applicants re-take required prerequisite coursework that is more than 5 years old from the anticipated date of matriculation..
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors:
The Thomas Haider Program at the UC Riverside School of Medicine, provides a unique pathway to admission into the UC Riverside School of Medicine by reserving up to 24 seats in each School of Medicine class for graduates who have completed at least six consecutive quarters of undergraduate study at UC Riverside. 

The UCR School of Medicine seeks students with diverse intellectual and life experiences. We value broad academic backgrounds that include humanities, foreign language, social sciences and the arts to help prepare future physicians for interacting with increasingly diverse patient populations, health care professionals and colleagues. Each applicant’s complete portfolio will be reviewed carefully in order to select students who are not only academically qualified but who have the breadth of volunteer, community and personal experiences to ensure that they will become physicians well prepared to care for the diverse population in our communities.
